rules.description: JWT authentication flow must remain operational.
rules.reason: JWT is detected as the active auth system. Changing or removing it invalidates all existing sessions.
rules.whatBreaks: All protected routes return 401. User sessions invalidated. Logout flows break.
examples: Do not swap JWT for a different auth library without a migration plan.
Do not remove auth middleware from protected routes.

rules.description: Authentication middleware (scripts/test_auth_consent_flow.mjs, src/context/AuthContext.tsx) must remain enabled on all protected routes.
rules.reason: These files guard access to protected resources. Disabling or bypassing them exposes all protected data.
rules.whatBreaks: Unauthorized users gain access to protected routes, user data, and admin features.
examples: Do not remove the auth check from scripts/test_auth_consent_flow.mjs.

rules.description: Firebase Auth authentication flow must remain operational.
rules.reason: Firebase Auth is detected as the active auth system. Changing or removing it invalidates all existing sessions.
rules.whatBreaks: All protected routes return 401. User sessions invalidated. Logout flows break.
examples: Do not swap Firebase Auth for a different auth library without a migration plan.
Do not remove auth middleware from protected routes.

rules.description: Authentication middleware (scripts/test_auth_consent_flow.mjs, scripts/unit/firebase_sync.test.mjs) must remain enabled on all protected routes.
rules.reason: These files guard access to protected resources. Disabling or bypassing them exposes all protected data.
rules.whatBreaks: Unauthorized users gain access to protected routes, user data, and admin features.
examples: Do not remove the auth check from scripts/test_auth_consent_flow.mjs.

rules.description: Services cannot import UI components.
rules.reason: Importing UI components into services couples server-side logic to browser rendering. This breaks SSR, testability, and separation of concerns.
rules.whatBreaks: Server-side services gain browser-only dependencies. Unit tests for services fail. SSR breaks.

rules.description: Controllers cannot access the database directly.
rules.reason: Direct DB access in controllers bypasses the service layer. This breaks the layered architecture and makes logic untestable.
rules.whatBreaks: Business logic leaks into controllers. Database coupling makes refactoring expensive.

rules.description: Route handlers cannot access the database directly.
rules.reason: Routes should delegate to services/controllers, not query the database themselves.
rules.whatBreaks: Business logic scattered across route files. Impossible to test in isolation.

rules.description: UI components cannot import server-only modules.
rules.reason: Server-only modules may contain secrets or Node.js-only APIs that crash in the browser.
rules.whatBreaks: Build errors in browser environments. Potential secret exposure.

rules.description: High-impact clusters (Other, Database, Config) must not gain new circular dependencies.
rules.reason: High-impact clusters already coordinate many modules. Adding circular imports makes builds fragile.
rules.whatBreaks: Module resolution fails. Build tools (webpack, esbuild) may hang or produce incorrect output.
examples: Use dependency injection or an event bus to break cycles.

rules.description: Password hashing algorithm must not be changed or removed.
rules.reason: The hashing algorithm is the last line of defence for stored credentials. Changing it invalidates all existing password hashes.
rules.whatBreaks: All existing users are locked out. Passwords unverifiable without a migration.

rules.description: Encryption implementation must remain algorithm-compatible.
rules.reason: Changing the encryption algorithm or key derivation method makes all existing encrypted data unreadable.
rules.whatBreaks: Encrypted data (tokens, at-rest fields, backups) cannot be decrypted.

rules.description: Environment secrets must never be hardcoded in source files.
rules.reason: Secrets committed to source are exposed via version control history and repository access.
rules.whatBreaks: Security breach. API keys, database credentials, and tokens compromised.

rules.description: Rate limiting must not be removed from public endpoints.
rules.reason: Rate limiting prevents brute-force attacks and denial-of-service.
rules.whatBreaks: Brute-force login attacks. API abuse. Service degradation under load.

rules.description: Environment variable files (.env) must never be committed to version control.
rules.reason: .env files contain secrets. Committing them exposes credentials to all repository users.
rules.whatBreaks: All secrets in .env become public. Immediate security incident.
examples: Use a secrets manager for production.

rules.description: Payment processing (PCI-DSS) — all Stripe/payment code requires compliance review.
rules.reason: PCI-DSS requires that all payment card data handling meets security standards. Any change to payment flows must be reviewed.
rules.whatBreaks: PCI compliance violation. Payment processor account suspension. Legal liability.
examples: Always review PCI-related code before merging.

rules.description: GDPR compliance — personal data handling must preserve user rights (consent, erasure, portability).
rules.reason: GDPR requires explicit consent for data collection, the right to erasure, and data portability. Removing these breaks legal compliance.
rules.whatBreaks: GDPR violation. Regulatory fines. User data rights cannot be exercised.
examples: Always review GDPR-related code before merging.

rules.description: HIPAA compliance — protected health information (PHI) handling must remain compliant.
rules.reason: HIPAA requires strict access control, audit logging, and encryption for all PHI. Removing protections is illegal.
rules.whatBreaks: HIPAA violation. Criminal liability. Patient data exposed.
examples: Always review HIPAA-related code before merging.

rules.description: Audit logging must always be written and never removed.
rules.reason: Audit logs provide the immutable record required for compliance, forensic investigation, and regulatory review.
rules.whatBreaks: Compliance audit failures. Inability to investigate security incidents. Regulatory violations.
examples: Always review AUDIT-related code before merging.

rules.description: Authentication Flow is repository-critical and must remain intact end-to-end.
rules.reason: Every protected page and authenticated feature depends on this flow working correctly.
rules.whatBreaks: Users cannot log in. All authenticated features become unreachable. Sessions invalidated.
examples: Do not change session token format without migration.

rules.description: User Registration Flow must remain functional. New users must be able to create accounts.
rules.reason: Registration is the entry point for all new users. Breaking it stops user growth.
rules.whatBreaks: New users cannot create accounts. User acquisition blocked.
examples: Do not change registration field requirements without versioning.

rules.description: Notification Pipeline (email, webhook, SMS) must remain operational.
rules.reason: Notifications are critical for transactional communication (receipts, alerts, order updates).
rules.whatBreaks: Users stop receiving transactional emails. Webhooks fail silently. Integrations break.
examples: Do not remove email delivery step from registration.
